content:
The [Body Surface Area Calculator](/body-surface-area-calculator) is a free online tool on CalcHub. Estimate adult body surface area with the Mosteller and Du Bois equations. Enter your weight and height and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. Because it runs entirely in your browser, the values you type never leave your device, and you can use it as often as you like.

Body surface area (BSA) estimates the external surface of the human body in square metres from height and weight. It appears in some physiological calculations and medication-dosing protocols because it can scale certain processes differently from body weight alone. This tool displays two widely used equations side by side, making their usually small difference visible instead of presenting a single formula as exact. This guide explains how to use it, the formula it applies, and a worked example you can follow with your own numbers.

## How to use the Body Surface Area Calculator

Start by entering your weight (kg), then entering your height (cm). The result updates as you type, so adjust any value and watch the answer change. If the answer is not what you expected, check the value you entered first — a missing digit or a wrong unit is the usual cause.

1. Measure height without shoes and enter it in centimetres.
2. Enter current weight in kilograms, using the measurement convention required by your clinical protocol.
3. Select the formula specified by the relevant protocol; do not average formulas unless there is a reason to do so.

## Formula

Mosteller BSA = √((height in cm × weight in kg) ÷ 3600). Du Bois BSA = 0.007184 × height^0.725 × weight^0.425.

That is the standard formula for this calculation, and it is the same one the [Body Surface Area Calculator](/body-surface-area-calculator) applies to the values you enter. You can work it out by hand, but the calculator is faster when you want to try several values, and it removes the risk of a slip in the arithmetic.

## Worked example

Here is a typical example. At 75 kg and 178 cm, Mosteller gives approximately 1.925 m² and Du Bois approximately 1.923 m². Small rounding differences are expected. Try the same figures in the [Body Surface Area Calculator](/body-surface-area-calculator) and you will get the same result — then change one value at a time to see how the answer moves.

## What the result shows

With the default values (Weight: 75 kg, Height: 178 cm), the [Body Surface Area Calculator](/body-surface-area-calculator) returns BSA — Mosteller: 1.926 m², BSA — Du Bois: 1.927 m², Average of the two estimates: 1.926 m², Weight × height used: 13,350 kg·cm. The first figure is the headline result, and the rest break it down so you can see how the total is made up. If you want to compare with a related calculation, the [BMI Calculator](/bmi-calculator) is worth a look before you finish.

## Mosteller and Du Bois equations

Mosteller is popular because its square-root expression is easy to calculate and remember. Du Bois is an older power equation derived from a small historical sample. Both are estimation models, not direct surface measurements. Modern clinical references may specify alternatives for particular populations or treatments.

## Clinical use requires the specified method

Some chemotherapy and other dosing references use BSA, but dosing also depends on the drug, diagnosis, organ function, age and protocol. A calculated BSA is only one input and should never be used to determine medication independently. Unusual body composition and paediatric use require particular professional care.

## Tips

A few things worth knowing before you rely on the result — most of them are about the numbers you put in, rather than the tool itself:

- Follow the equation named in any clinical worksheet or protocol.
- Use consistent metric units; entering pounds or inches directly will produce an invalid result.
- Keep several decimal places during later calculations and round only at the final required step.

## Frequently asked questions

### Which BSA formula is best?

Mosteller is widely used for its simplicity, but the best formula is the one required by the applicable protocol. No equation is exact for every body shape and population. You can see it in action in the [Body Surface Area Calculator](/body-surface-area-calculator) — enter your own values and the result updates as you type.

### What is average body surface area?

Many references quote roughly 1.7–1.9 m² for adults, but BSA varies substantially with height and weight, so an individual calculation is more useful. Try it with your own numbers in the [Body Surface Area Calculator](/body-surface-area-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### Can I use this to calculate medication?

Not on your own. Medication dosing requires a clinician or pharmacist and the correct protocol, with checks that go beyond BSA. Try it with your own numbers in the [Body Surface Area Calculator](/body-surface-area-calculator) — the result updates as you type, so you can test a few scenarios in seconds.

### What do I need to use the Body Surface Area Calculator?

Just Weight and Height. Enter those values and the result appears straight away — no account or download needed. If you are unsure about a value, try a rough figure first and then refine it — the result updates instantly.
